mutants.name: live-arm-does-not-seed-the-frontier
mutants.//: #193 inc 2. armGaplessLive flips the flag and stops there, which is what an ordinary setGapless(true) would do. maybeAppendNext's one-ahead test (appendedThrough_ == trackIndex_) then refuses forever with appendedThrough_ still -1, so a queue that grew from one track silently keeps the gap #141 removed - and nothing is red, because the track still plays, just late.
mutants.find:
prevPos_ = 0;                    // mpv holds the one entry its last replace-load gave it
    appendedThrough_ = trackIndex_;  // …which is the playing entry: its successor is the frontier to feed

mutants.name: live-arm-re-seeds-a-frontier-that-is-already-live
mutants.//: #193 inc 2. The refusal when gapless is ALREADY on is dropped, so a second arm resets the frontier back onto the playing entry and the entry mpv was already handed is appended a second time - the one-ahead invariant broken by the thing meant to bootstrap it.

mutants.name: live-arm-arms-with-nothing-playing
mutants.//: #193 inc 2. With no cursor there is no entry to seed the frontier onto; arming anyway points the feed at index -1.

mutants.name: an-edit-announces-itself-as-a-brand-new-queue
mutants.//: #193 inc 3. The host presents a now-playing surface for a REPLACED queue. Say it for an edit and every browse-side 'add to queue' yanks the listener off the row they are standing on and onto the player - the exact state increment 2's Append arm exists to avoid, and one nothing else in this probe can see.
mutants.find: emit queueChanged(titles_, trackIndex_, /*replaced*/ false);   // an EDIT: present nothing
mutants.replace: emit queueChanged(titles_, trackIndex_, /*replaced*/ true);   // an EDIT: present nothing

mutants.name: deleting-the-playing-track-announces-a-brand-new-queue
mutants.//: #193 inc 3. commitEdit's cursorRemoved branch is a SECOND queueChanged emit and can be forgotten on its own.
mutants.find: emit queueChanged(titles_, plan.playIndex, /*replaced*/ false);   // an EDIT: present nothing
mutants.replace: emit queueChanged(titles_, plan.playIndex, /*replaced*/ true);   // an EDIT: present nothing

mutants.name: installing-a-queue-announces-itself-as-a-mere-edit
mutants.//: #193 inc 3. The other direction, and the worse one: a deliberate play that presents NOTHING. The music starts, the page never opens, and the user is left on the row they pressed Play on with sound coming from nowhere.
mutants.find: emit queueChanged(titles_, startIndex, /*replaced*/ true);   // a whole new queue: the host may present it
mutants.replace: emit queueChanged(titles_, startIndex, /*replaced*/ false);   // a whole new queue: the host may present it
